name: Ulster loyalism
summary: Ulster loyalism is the working-class Protestant strand of Ulster unionism. It holds that Northern Ireland must remain in the United Kingdom under the Crown, opposes Irish unification and Irish nationalism, and defends Protestant British culture, parades and flags. It has a paramilitary wing that justified violence in defence of the Union, and a political wing that shifted to political means after the 1994 ceasefires.
scope: Mainstream post-1960s loyalism as expressed by the UVF, UDA, the PUP and UDP, the Loyalist Communities Council and the Orange tradition, with roots in the 1912 Covenant and Edward Carson, and Paisleyite fundamentalism as an adjacent influence. Economic and moral issues are mostly inferred, since loyalism has no systematic programme beyond the Union and identity. Mainstream unionist parties are not the basis.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Loyalists took the Allied side in WWII and are anti-communist and anti-republican; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Loyalists accept the mainstream historical view; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Preserving Union flags, memorials and parades is the loyalist cause; see the flag and parade positions already recorded.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Loyalism holds with British institutions and doesn't discuss civilizations; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Loyalism relies on the British army and police but opposes military rule; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not a loyalist concern; the movement has no stated position on recognising unpaid care as labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the Orange and Paisleyite social conservatism and Protestant family values.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's attachment to elected government under the Crown; no examination-based selection is documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Loyalist politics span the left-of-centre PUP to conservative unionism; no common position on foreign buyers is documented.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Orange Order's conservatism and Paisley's fundamentalist social conservatism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's attachment to the Westminster parliamentary system; no mandate or recall tradition is documented.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the working-class base and the PUP's left-of-centre politics, which favour state welfare provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, property-owning tradition; no loyalist strand argues for communal land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's attachment to parliamentary government and the Covenant's constitutional language.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from loyalist identity politics, which treats English as the common language and resists elevating Irish.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not an issue loyalism addresses and no position can be inferred from its principles.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the conservative Orange tradition, which resists equality measures aimed at group outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not an issue loyalism addresses; no position is documented.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's own opposition to republican insurgency and its stress on law and the state.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's insistence on majority consent for constitutional status.

corporate-influence.rationale: Adherents are split: the working-class PUP is left of centre, but other loyalists align with business unionism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from loyalist hostility to outside political influence and Irish nationalist funding, though no funding policy is documented.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Adherents are split; Paisleyite moral conservatives favour family policy while the PUP is more liberal, and no common stance is documented.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not a loyalist issue; the PUP leans left on housing and the Protestant working class, but no position on residents-only purchases is documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the PUP's left-of-centre working-class politics, though job guarantees are not documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to the British state and Western alliance, but the issue is not documented.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Loyalism is built on loyalty to the Crown and the 1912 Covenant's pledge, and treats the Union and law as binding, though paramilitaries claimed violence was justified.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from its self-image of defending the Union against Dublin interference, but outside intervention by Britain is welcomed.

industrial-unions.rationale: Adherents are split; the PUP is union-friendly and working class, but no position on industrial versus craft unions is documented.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Loyalism casts Irish nationalism and Catholicism as a threat to the Protestant community, and the Orange Order excludes Catholics. No cited source documents a belief in a secret conspiracy, so the answer is inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Orange and Paisleyite traditions are socially conservative and defend the traditional family and marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Adherents are split and the issue is not documented; loyalism has no defined position on freedom of information.

local-production.rationale: Not a loyalist issue and no position is documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: Loyalism is organised through formal bodies: the Orange Order, UVF, UDA and parties such as the PUP.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Loyalists reject outside courts and European bodies over the sovereignty of the UK, and the PUP objected to the Protocol.

religious-nation.rationale: The Orange Order and Paisleyite tradition define the community as Protestant, and loyalism is described as a Protestant British identity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: loyalism is loyal to the Crown and the Union but has no tradition of tribute or ritual submission among states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: Northern Ireland relies on UK-wide transfers, and loyalism values the Union's pooled resources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from a working-class strand that accepts private property alongside left-of-centre social policy.

defeat-communism.rationale: Loyalism's enemy is Irish republicanism, not communism, and its political wing is left of centre, so adherents are split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the PUP's social-democratic line and loyalist defence of the NHS as a state institution.

religion-illusion.rationale: Loyalism is bound to Protestant religion and the Orange tradition, which treat faith as central to identity and enduring.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: a British-identifying strand that values the industrial and imperial economy of the UK.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the PUP is left of centre, but loyalism has no feminist economic programme and tends to social conservatism.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from a socially conservative, family-centred culture.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: loyalism defends English-language British culture and has no language-purity agenda.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: loyalism distrusts agreements that limit the Union and favours majority consent over fixed treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: loyalism is committed to the UK state and Crown, not to self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: historic plantation settlement is part of loyalist identity, but no modern policy of promoting it is documented.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: loyalism sits within British democratic capitalism and has no third-way doctrine.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: loyalism rests its case on majority consent and British identity rather than on historical land claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: loyalism has no association with Holocaust denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Split: Paisleyite fundamentalism opposed decriminalisation, but loyalism has no systematic position and working-class loyalists vary.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: the 1994 ceasefire statement commits to peaceful, political conflict, though loyalists have suppressed nationalist opposition by violence in practice.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Split: Paisleyite fundamentalists favour it, but most working-class loyalists do not.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the Crown's overseas territories are not a loyalist concern.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: loyalism is Protestant and unionist, and the doctrine is not part of its tradition.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from its loyalty to the Crown and constitutional order (the Covenant pledges loyalty to the Crown).

participatory-democracy.rationale: Split: the PUP stresses community politics while the broader tradition is hierarchical and Orange-lodge-based.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from its focus on communal British Protestant identity over class-race-gender analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Protestant social conservatism, Orange Order and Paisleyite influence.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Split: the Union comes first, with the PUP's socialist wing set against conservative unionism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Split: PUP socialism accepts parts of the critique, while most adherents never address it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; loyalist hostility is directed at Irish Catholic nationalism rather than Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the 1912 Covenant's appeal to Almighty God and the Protestant fundamentalist strand (Paisley).

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Split: Protestant culture and symbols are defended, but the issue is not addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: Split: the PUP is social-democratic, while most loyalists follow no economic program.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from its strong attachment to the British Crown and state, including the British Army, and paramilitary self-image.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from working-class, egalitarian loyalist politics (PUP).

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from its unionist loyalty to the UK, a NATO state.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's devotion to the Crown, which carries hereditary monarchy; the statement is about leaders of states generally, so the support is indirect.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: loyalism has no banking program, and the PUP's left-leaning social democracy is not about user-owned credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; the PUP's left-leaning strand might agree while loyalism's UK-centred stance leaves it indifferent to IMF conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: the Covenant and loyalism's working-class base favour broad participation, and the PUP is social democratic.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed; loyalism has no stance on ecofeminist theory, and its culture is socially conservative, so this is inferred indifference.

reification.rationale: Inferred: the PUP's social-democratic line sometimes echoes Marxist-flavoured class critique, but loyalism overall rejects Marxist social theory.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; the working-class PUP strand might agree about wealth, but loyalism as a whole has no press position.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: the Covenant pledged defence of 'equal citizenship' and British constitutional order, which favours law-based government, though loyalist paramilitaries acted outside the law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Loyalism is built on British Protestant identity but claims citizenship within the UK for all; the PUP and ceasefire statement did not seek to limit the franchise by ethnicity.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; loyalism takes no position on online participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; loyalism takes no position on open government data.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: Orange and Paisleyite loyalism is hostile to Roman Catholicism and has historically opposed mixed marriage, though mainstream adherents mostly do not seek legal restriction.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: loyalists have occasionally boycotted Catholic-owned businesses, but the PUP and ceasefire statement rejected sectarianism, so a typical adherent would not endorse it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's defence of established Crown and parliamentary institutions and its reliance on referendums and elected bodies on the Union; lot-chosen assemblies are not discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from the Protestant fundamentalism of Paisleyism and the Orange tradition, which hold to inherited Reformation doctrine rather than modernising it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Progressive Unionist Party's left-of-centre, working-class politics, which is wary of concentrated economic power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from Paisleyite fundamentalist opposition to homosexuality, an adjacent influence on loyalist culture; not a core loyalist issue.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Loyalism defends Protestant British culture and the Orange tradition, which are religious; state atheism is alien to it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's law-and-order, pro-state stance in defence of the Union, though some loyalists distrust the police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The PUP and UDP backed the 1998 power-sharing settlement, though other unionists opposed it; inferred from their political turn after the ceasefires.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the PUP's social-democratic outlook, which favours public provision for working-class communities over charity.

term-limits.rationale: Loyalism has no stated position on term limits; inferred as indifferent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's attachment to traditional Westminster-style representative institutions; delegation is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by loyalism; no principle to infer from.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from Paisley's Free Presbyterian tradition and Protestant fundamentalist church practice, where ministry is male; adherents may differ.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from conservative Protestant norms, which are mixed on marital headship, and from loyalism's silence on the matter.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not a loyalist issue; inferred from its emphasis on British citizenship and the British state as the basis of belonging.

rent-control.rationale: The PUP, the main loyalist party, is left of centre and working class, which makes support for housing protections likely.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's conservative attachment to property and established law.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Loyalist culture has long been organised through uniformed bodies such as the Orange Order, bands and the old volunteer tradition of the Covenant; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from its pro-British, pro-defence stance; the matter does not arise because no such weapons are in Northern Ireland.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its loyalty to the British armed forces and the Crown; allied bases would not be seen as an offence.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not part of loyalism; adherents hold no common view on genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The PUP and working-class loyalism have stressed the interests of workers over those of capital, inferred from its programme.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Loyalist paramilitaries justified violence in defence of the Union and their community, and the ceasefire statement speaks of defence of the loyalist people.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Loyalism roots identity in British and Ulster-Scots history and the 1912 Covenant rather than in ancient continuity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the Paisleyite, fundamentalist Protestant influence on loyalist culture, which holds fixed sexes.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the same fundamentalist Protestant influence; feminist identity politics is foreign to it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Loyalist culture honours its dead and murals commemorate fallen volunteers; the language of martyrs is used within the tradition.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Paisleyite fundamentalism frames politics as the defence of Protestantism against Rome, though mainstream loyalism is more secular; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Loyalism is tied to the Northern Ireland and British state, not to a dispersed people; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Loyalism has put the constitutional position first, culture being defended within it; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the conservative Protestant churches that shape loyalist culture and Paisley's tradition.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the same conservative Protestant tradition, which reads scripture by its own authority.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Loyalism claims British rights for all citizens, though its history includes Protestant dominance; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The loyalist aim is to keep the present borders of Northern Ireland within the UK, not to merge regions by people; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred, not documented: working-class loyalism and the PUP have a labour tradition of independent unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred, not documented: the PUP is social democratic, but the question is not a loyalist concern and adherents are split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred, not documented: the base depends on the NHS and local public services, and the PUP is left of centre.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalists favour the British parliamentary tradition, which includes the House of Lords.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalism has no municipal-ownership programme and favours the UK state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalism defends the UK union with decisions taken by sovereign Westminster, not a confederal model.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred, not documented: the working-class and socially conservative base and the PUP's left-of-centre stance favour this.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred, not documented: no stated position; adherents are split.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred, not documented: no stated position; adherents are split.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalists back security-first measures against terrorism, which cuts against untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred, not documented: security-first outlook, and loyalists have been wary of anonymity that shields opponents.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred, not documented: Protestant individualism and loyalty to the Crown and community pull in different directions; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred, not documented: the Orange tradition and Paisleyite fundamentalism are strongly religious, so adherents hold that politics should serve spiritual life.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's defence of the Union: Northern Ireland's devolved powers rest on Westminster, which is sovereign and can suspend them, as in the Home Rule opposition and the Covenant.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred, not documented: no stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred, not documented: no stated position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalism is defined by Protestant British identity and religion, not by race, so it does not frame politics on racial lines.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalist pride is in British and Protestant identity and heritage rather than race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalists identify with the British armed forces and accepted a role for force in defence of the Union, so a strict ban on starting wars is not their stance.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Loyalism rejects an all-island Irish nation despite the shared Irish language and history; it defines belonging by Crown and Union.

communal-electorates.rationale: Loyalism insists on equal citizenship under the Crown and wants one common electorate within the UK, though power-sharing designations are accepted in practice.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Loyalists have long treated Irish nationalism and Dublin's role, and later the Protocol, as threats to the Union; inferred from this mistrust.

free-public-college.rationale: Loyalism has no systematic programme on education; the PUP is left-of-centre but the wider movement is not documented as taking a side.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Loyalism has no documented position on environmental taxation.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, stewardship-minded Protestant and Orange tradition; not a documented priority.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the Orange Order's and Paisleyite social conservatism; no documented line on women's distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Loyalist paramilitaries were committed to armed defence of the Union and resisted decommissioning; inferred from this, with the ceasefire statement conditional.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Loyalists complained of secret deals over the Anglo-Irish Agreement and the Protocol, so openness is inferred as favoured.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from its conservative, pro-UK establishment orientation; no documented position on capital controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Loyalist paramilitaries, from the 1912 UVF onward, were justified as defenders of the Union and kept arms through the ceasefire era, so adherents resist the claim that only state forces may bear arms; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Loyalism is rooted in loyalty to the Crown and the British Army tradition, so refusing orders to fight in the state's wars runs against its core.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The PUP, the main loyalist party, is left of centre and working class, so union bargaining is inferred as favoured.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Working-class loyalism and the social-democratic PUP are inferred to back state top-ups for low-paid families.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Loyalism has no fiscal programme; the PUP leans left while unionist parties lean conservative, so adherents are inferred to be split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not a loyalist issue; inferred from a UK-centred, insular working-class outlook that is sceptical of foreign aid-style redistribution.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Loyalism defends the existing British state and constitution, so it rejects smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Loyalism never addressed economic pluralism; no stated position, so left neutral.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not an issue loyalism addresses; no basis to infer a direction.

sacred-nation.rationale: Loyalism treats the Union, the Crown and Protestant British culture as a covenanted community, as in the 1912 Covenant; the sacred framing is inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Loyalism has no stated position; the PUP's left lean and unionist conservatism point in opposite directions.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Loyalists reject nationalist narratives of British colonial exploitation of Ireland, though they feel neglected by elites; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Loyalism's Protestant fundamentalist strand, as with Paisley, holds a Christian view of fixed human nature; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Loyalists defend British institutions such as the BBC; inferred rather than documented.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Loyalism is rooted in Protestant, Orange and Paisleyite tradition that treats Protestantism as the true faith and Catholicism as erroneous, not as one truth among many.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: loyalism has no farm policy, but its left-of-centre working-class party favours state support for livelihoods.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's strong British, Crown and military loyalty, which backs the UK keeping its deterrent.

workers-own-party.rationale: The PUP and UDP arose as working-class loyalist parties distinct from the middle-class Ulster Unionists.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: loyalists accept UK law, which prohibits FGM, and the issue is not contested within loyalism.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: equal property rights for women are settled UK law that loyalists uphold as British citizens.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: loyalists promote Ulster Scots as a distinct language and resist treating it as part of an Irish-language framework, so they favour separate names and status.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: loyalists accept the UK's agency-based regulatory state and have no tradition of tort-only environmental law.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: loyalism defends Crown-in-Parliament sovereignty and has no customary chiefs to give a role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: not a loyalist concern; its identity politics centres on liberty to parade and preserve culture rather than environmental limits.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the law-and-order, pro-security stance of loyalists and Paisleyite fundamentalism.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred: loyalism's emphasis on British national identity supports expecting newcomers to learn English.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: the PUP is left of centre and union-friendly, while the broader loyalist base is mixed.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: unionists generally back ID checks, and loyalism shares the concern with electoral integrity.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: loyalism defends civil and religious liberty for Protestants against Catholic or Irish nationalist dominance, so favours equal standing.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the consent principle in the 1994 ceasefire statement and the Covenant's appeal to democratic majority.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the Protestant fundamentalist and Orange influences, not a documented statement.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: it is a law-and-order strand but defends civil liberties as British subjects; no documented position.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the PUP is social democratic and favours existing public welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: women's equal political rights are settled in the UK, which loyalism defends.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the Orange and Paisleyite Protestant tradition, which defends religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred, not documented: loyalism has no stated line on the nature of race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: the PUP is progressive on this, but the wider loyalist base is conservative.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Loyalism has no programme on property theory, and the working-class and PUP strands differ from market-minded unionists.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the loyalist view that outside bodies have no standing over Ulster affairs, and its paramilitary history.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the strong Protestant evangelical culture around the Orange tradition and Paisleyism, though the question is not stated as a loyalist position.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative, male-led culture of the loyalist and Orange tradition.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's anti-communist, pro-British stance, though the PUP leans social-democratic.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the loyalist reliance on direct popular votes and the consent of the majority.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the Orange Order's commitment to the Protestant faith and the Protestant Crown, so the loyalist tradition favours Protestant privilege in state religion.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from loyalist support for Northern Ireland's devolved government, where a unionist majority holds regional power.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The consent principle, that Northern Ireland's status changes only if a majority votes for it, is stated in the 1994 loyalist ceasefire statement and PUP policy.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the loyalist defence of the 1921 partition border and the Covenant's refusal to be placed under an Irish parliament.

simple-living.rationale: Loyalism has no stated view on simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's opposition to any protected status for Irish nationalist communities and its demand for equal British rights.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription was never imposed in Northern Ireland and loyalists hold both pro-military and traditional-gender views, so adherents are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Loyalist identity stresses attachment to Ulster and its Protestant British heritage as something to defend, but not in explicitly spiritual terms; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Loyalist paramilitaries killed alleged dealers outside the law, but support for state killing without trial is not a stated position; adherents are split.

close-ties-china.rationale: Loyalism is strongly British and Atlanticist in orientation, so a pivot toward China is unlikely; inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Loyalism has no stated policy on kin minorities abroad; Protestant minorities in the Irish Republic are only occasionally mentioned.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Property-owning working-class Protestants and the Orange tradition lean toward conventional property rights; the PUP's left stance makes this a mild inference.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; loyalism has no systematic doctrine on this.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is not a loyalist concern and the PUP's left-leaning economics versus other strands makes adherents split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The PUP, the main loyalist party, is social democratic and supports universal welfare protections; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Loyalism is organised through parties, the Orange Order and community councils, and defends parliamentary Union institutions; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Loyalism has not made this a defining issue; adherents are split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Loyalism is explicitly tied to Protestant identity and the Orange Order, which organises politics along denominational lines.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; Paisleyite religious conservatism sits against a secular PUP, so adherents are split.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Paisleyite fundamentalists would oppose it and the PUP might not; adherents are split.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource control is not a defining issue; loyalists favour UK-wide governance of resources, but this is inferred only weakly.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Loyalism has no distributive doctrine; inferred at low confidence from its defence of property and tradition, though the PUP wing is social democratic.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Loyalism has no stated position, and the PUP's left-leaning strand differs from the conservative unionist base.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: loyalists tend to see Protestant working-class communities as the disadvantaged group and discount the claim that racism is the chief obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Loyalists defend the rule of law and the consent principle, though paramilitaries justified violence against what they saw as illegitimate settlements; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Loyalism has no recorded view on automation, and the PUP's working-class concern for jobs pulls against it.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from loyalism's loyalty to the British Crown and the United Kingdom, which favours one state over independent centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The PUP is democratic socialist in tradition, but loyalism as a whole has no Marxist value theory; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Loyalism is working-class Protestant unionism that ties British patriotism to working-class interests, and the PUP drew on that link.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: loyalism puts the constitutional question and Protestant British identity first, ahead of left cultural politics, though the PUP is socially concerned.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: loyalism opposes communist rule and supports British parliamentary democracy.

missingStatements.text: A region's constitutional status should change only if a majority of its people vote for it.
missingStatements.rationale: The consent principle underlies the 1994 ceasefire statement and the PUP's later objection to the Protocol.

missingStatements.text: Communities should be free to hold traditional parades along customary routes, even through areas where residents object.
missingStatements.rationale: Loyalists see parade restrictions as attacks on their cultural identity; the Orange Order's Drumcree marches are the best-known example.

missingStatements.text: The national flag should be flown over public buildings as a symbol of the state.
missingStatements.rationale: Loyalists treat restrictions on the Union Flag as attacks on their identity.

notes: Loyalists split on moral issues (the PUP is more liberal than Paisleyites) and on the economy; the paramilitary strand was more violent than the political strand. Many answers are inferred with low confidence.
